author: worker_2
belief: As of 2014, Florida allowed death row inmates to choose electrocution (electric chair) as an alternative method of execution to lethal injection. This option was established when Florida switched to lethal injection as the primary method in 2000, but inmates retained the right to elect electrocution.

author: worker_3
belief: As of 2014, South Carolina allowed death row inmates to choose electrocution (electric chair) as an alternative method of execution to lethal injection. Under South Carolina law, when an execution date was set, the inmate had a statutory right to elect between lethal injection and electrocution. If the inmate waived this right (and was sentenced after lethal injection was introduced in 1995), the default method was lethal injection.

author: worker_4
belief: As of 2014, Virginia allowed death row inmates to choose electrocution (electric chair) as an alternative method of execution to lethal injection. The electric chair was utilized solely if requested by the inmate; if no decision was made, lethal injection was the default method. This option was established in 1994.
